section_1.title: The Root Problem: Filtering Coefficients
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of finding the sum of every k-th coefficient in a generating function P(x). Use the visual concept of a 'filter' that eliminates unwanted terms. Prerequisites: Euler’s Formula (e^ix = cos x + i sin x) and the definition of the n-th roots of unity (ω^k).
section_1.example: A squirrel gathering nuts in piles of size 0, 3, 6... how to sum coefficients of x^3k in (1+x)^n.

section_2.title: The Roots of Unity Filter Lemma
section_2.content: Explain the identity: 1/n * Σ (ω^j)^k = 1 if n divides k, and 0 otherwise. Visualize this as a 'rotating vector sum' in the complex plane where vectors cancel out unless they align at the origin.
section_2.example: Visualize the 4th roots of unity (1, i, -1, -i) as points on a unit circle. Show how their sum equals zero, acting as a perfect zero-balance scale.

section_3.title: Step-by-Step Implementation
section_3.content: Demonstrate the procedure: 1. Identify the generating function P(x). 2. Evaluate P(x) at ω^j. 3. Average the results: 1/n * Σ P(ω^j). Use a flow-chart animation to move from the function to the complex evaluation.
section_3.example: Calculating the sum of binomial coefficients Σ C(n, 3k) by evaluating (1+ω^j)^n for the 3rd roots of unity.

section_4.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
section_4.content: Conclude by mapping the algebraic result back to the complex plane. Highlight that complex numbers transform a 'picking' operation into a 'geometric cancellation' operation. Quick recap of the 5-minute flow.
section_4.example: Final slide showing a 'Robot Collector' selecting every 4th item from a conveyor belt by applying a complex filter.
